extracted.intended_audience: mathematics faculty, department chairs, assessment coordinators, and university administrators involved in undergraduate mathematics programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reported practices for designing, administering, and evaluating undergraduate mathematics placement, advisement, and quantitative literacy assessment programs at universities. Includes test design, placement policy, advising structures, assessment instruments, and use of data for curricular change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test formats and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Students choose between two timed multiple-choice tests adopted from the 1993 California Mathematics Diagnostic Testing project: Test A (50-minute, 45-question covering intermediate algebra skills) and Test B (90-minute, 60-question covering college algebra and trigonometry skills).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test A places students into one of three algebra levels or a liberal arts math course; Test B places into finite mathematics, pre-calculus, or calculus levels. Tests were administered during mandatory two-day summer orientation sessions and during other times throughout the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculator and device policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The version currently being used allows a variety of calculators (including graphing calculators). For test securing reasons, those with QWERTY keyboards are not allowed at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish explicit allowed/disallowed device rules to preserve test security and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic scoring and rapid feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The tests are scored electronically, and results are printed that evening. Each student receives a profile sheet indicating their mathematics placement and a breakdown of their total score by topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prompt results (e.g., next morning) to integrate with advising/registration; group questions into topic areas (7–8 areas such as linear functions, simplifying expressions) so students receive diagnostic feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement registration controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Students may register for courses at their level or lower. The computerized registration process blocks students from registering for courses at a higher level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use registration system constraints to enforce placement decisions and prevent inappropriate higher-level enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-factor placement decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Although placement is initially based on a test score, other factors are considered (e.g., high school GPA automatically considered for freshmen whose scores fall near a cut-off; transfer students allowed to use prerequisite coursework). The coordinator makes final decisions when overriding any initial placement based on test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine objective test scores with academic history and coordinator/advisor discretion for borderline cases; document override policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut-off score setting and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum or cut-off scores were initially based on historical (optional test) data and are monitored periodically and adjusted if needed. Goal: set a cut-off score that minimizes the errors on either side of the cut-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical success-rate data at each level to choose appropriate GPA/cut-off values; periodically re-evaluate cut-offs, especially when curricula change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot placement via standardized test scores
rubrics_metrics.description: A pilot placement program allowed freshmen to place into calculus based on high recentered SAT (RSAT) or ACT mathematics scores without taking Test B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot alternate placement pathways and measure concordance with the main test (e.g., 91% agreement reported in pilot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retake and appeals policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally students take the wrong test and may take the correct test on the second day. These tests (hand-scored) generally cannot be taken more than once within any three-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish retake frequency limits to reduce frivolous appeals and administrative burden; accommodate genuine misadministered-test cases via limited immediate retake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of topic-level diagnostic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Each profile sheet provides a breakdown of total score by topic area so students and advisors can see strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use item/topic breakdowns to inform advising, remedial supports, and curriculum adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinator-driven monitoring and annual analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the year the coordinator monitors numbers of students placing at each level, assists advisors with placement issues, distributes information to outside groups, and conducts end-of-year analyses of the placement procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized monitoring (program coordinator) supports continuous quality improvement and communication with stakeholders (high schools, community colleges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of minimizing misplacement errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The program's goal is not to set an unreasonably high cut-off that would deny registration to a student with a reasonable chance for success; instead, choose cut-offs that minimize errors on either side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance false-positives and false-negatives using measured course success rates to inform decisions rather than aiming for high pass percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory testing for large-scale programs
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no room for flexibility with regard to mandatory testing and forced placement for very large entry-level populations; an optional test would be ineffective with 5,000 students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large, diverse cohorts, mandatory standardized placement ensures consistent placement and advisement data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support and resource commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong support by the department and university is crucial (cooperation of administrators, faculty, and students). Funding and manpower are major obstacles; the coordinator and advisors must be funded, and the coordinator may receive a course reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure funding, staff time, and administrative buy-in; recognize/compensate coordinator and advisors to sustain program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear communication with external partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing communication with high schools and local colleges is imperative; misinformation or lack of information can undermine program credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively distribute information and findings to counselors, teachers, and feeder schools to align expectations and placement preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and continuity in appeals and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: While there are guidelines (test scores, prerequisite courses, GPA), a more subjective set of guidelines may be necessary to handle individual cases; continuity is important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design appeals procedures that allow documented exceptions, but keep consistent records and rationales to preserve program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early advisor-advisee connection and resource provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective majors are advised by a department faculty member in a summer orientation and counseling session; students are given a Guide for the Mathematics Major containing degree requirements, course descriptions, faculty bios, and a five-year plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish advisor relationships early (pre-arrival/orientation) and provide clear written guidance to students and families to support retention and informed course selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of automated degree-audit tools to free advisor time
rubrics_metrics.description: The college uses the PACE (Programmed Academic Curriculum Evaluation) degree audit and advisement tool which updates course results, GPAs, credit completed, and remaining requirements, freeing advisors from bookkeeping tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement degree-audit systems so advisors can focus on substantive advising (career goals, research, performance) rather than record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor program and proactive outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: A Freshman Mentor Program matches students with volunteer mentors from the college, includes planned group activities, and proactively contacts non-applicants by phone to encourage participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a mixture of social events, panels, and active recruitment to increase mentor program uptake and early student engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental tutoring and learning centers
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are kept on track by graduate students, undergraduate majors, and faculty who provide tutorial assistance in a departmentally sponsored Mathematics Learning Center and a Calculus Lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide structured drop-in and scheduled tutoring support connected to courses to improve pass rates and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor training and standardized materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All department advisors are given a copy of the college’s Academic Advisor’s Handbook and attend fall advisement workshops conducted by the Dean’s Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train advisors annually and supply standardized handbooks to maintain consistent advising quality across faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, multi-method program assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing assessment mechanisms include: mailing surveys to majors at 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20 years after graduation; requiring graduating seniors to complete questionnaires; querying faculty during annual reviews; collecting unsolicited student comments; surveying mentor program participants; and conducting exit interviews with students who withdraw during a semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple instruments and timepoints (short-term, longitudinal, alumni) to triangulate program effectiveness and obtain actionable feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and workload design to sustain advising
rubrics_metrics.description: Reward and recognition for faculty participation are crucial; remove most record-keeping tasks from advisors so they can devote interactions to substantive issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design workload reductions, incentives, and recognition structures to promote sustained faculty engagement in advising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of assessment findings to target improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment data are discussed in appropriate forums and used to modify program components, change recognition/reward structures, and identify issues such as attracting non-participants or addressing transfer-student needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate assessment results into concrete action plans (outreach strategies, advisory committees, targeted interventions) and monitor outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative literacy competency statements (MAA/CUPM)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantitatively literate college graduate should be able to: (1) Interpret mathematical models such as formulas, graphs, tables, and schematics, and draw inferences from them; (2) Represent mathematical information symbolically, visually, numerically, and verbally; (3) Use arithmetical, algebraic, geometric and statistical methods to solve problems; (4) Estimate and check answers to determine reasonableness, identify alternatives, and select optimal results; (5) Recognize that mathematical and statistical methods have limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt these competency goals as desired learning outcomes for general-education quantitative literacy programs; align courses and assessments to measure each capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program design: foundations plus continuation experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: CUPM recommends programs consist of a foundations experience to introduce patterns of thought and mathematical resources, plus continuation experiences to reinforce and practice habits of thinking over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure curricula so students receive an initial explicit foundations course and subsequent reinforcement across majors and service courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple routes to meet competency with evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish multiple ways by which the competency requirement can be met (e.g., Core Competency course; Elementary Functions; Foundations of Elementary School Mathematics; Finite Math; Calculus for Business and Social Science; Calculus I) but require evidence that each route leads to at least minimal competency. The department determined these courses satisfy competency objectives provided a student completed such a course with a grade of at least a C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow multiple approved courses to fulfill the requirement, but set a minimum-grade threshold and periodically verify via assessments that each route attains the intended competency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment test design for quantitative literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests consisted of multiple comparable forms administered near the end of the semester: ten multiple-choice questions (computational facility), three open-ended interpretive questions, and three problems to solve. Exams were graded with a uniform standard; passing was set at attainment of at least 50% of the possible score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design multi-component assessments (MCQ for computation, open response for interpretation, problems for problem solving), use common grading rubrics, and set explicit passing criteria tied to competency expectations. Attach grade incentives to ensure student effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of item analysis and statistical monitoring of test forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Item analysis was recommended to help construct improved placement tests and a senior follow-up test; comparable multiple forms can produce unevenness, so using forms in more than one course and statistics to compare results should 'flag' a bad form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform item-level analysis and cross-form statistics to detect inconsistent forms; revise items or forms flagged by analysis. Limit reliance on many distinct multiple-choice forms unless quality-equating procedures are in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance multiple-choice versus open-ended items given grading resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple-choice questions were used on the computational facility part of the test merely to save time in grading; when fewer students are being examined, multiple-choice can be eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose item types according to available grading resources and desired construct validity; prefer open-ended items for problem solving when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment-informed curricular refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment results led to specific curricular actions (e.g., bolster problem solving in Elementary Functions; bolster computational facility in Foundations of Elementary School Mathematics) and to no change in the C-grade requirement for competency credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use disaggregated assessment data to identify course-level weaknesses and implement targeted curriculum changes, then reassess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and staffing considerations for assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment process required substantial effort: organizing exams, preparing multiple forms, and staffing graders (team of five graders plus course instructors for some sections). The process was organized to be minimally intrusive for individual courses and instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan adequate staff/time for large-scale assessment projects and design administration to minimize disruption to normal course delivery.
